question.:question/problem:
$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}-6 & -3 & -2 \\ -8 & 8 & 10 \\ -2 & 0 & -10\end{bmatrix},\,B=\begin{bmatrix}0 & -3 & 28 \\ 0 & 8 & 50 \\ -2 & 0 & -10\end{bmatrix}
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form $R_{i}:=R_{i}+kR_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above $a_{31}=-2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}-6 & -3 & -2 \\ -8 & 8 & 10 \\ -2 & 0 & -10\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{1}:=R_{1}-3R_{3}}\begin{bmatrix}0 & -3 & 28 \\ -8 & 8 & 10 \\ -2 & 0 & -10\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{2}:=R_{2}-4R_{3}}\begin{bmatrix}0 & -3 & 28 \\ 0 & 8 & 50 \\ -2 & 0 & -10\end{bmatrix}=B
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$R_{1}:=R_{1}-3R_{3}$ and $R_{2}:=R_{2}-4R_{3}$.
